chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-Baḥrayn, where he shed the blood of some people from among the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians. He then wrote to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: “I have shed the blood of some people from among the Jews and the Christians, so I paid their blood money as eight hundred, eight hundred; and I have shed the blood of some people from among the Magians, but you had not given me any prior instruction concerning them.”

He said: So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله wrote to him: “Indeed, their blood money is like the blood money of the Jews and the Christians,” and he said: “Indeed, they are People of the Book.”

key_terms.أَهْلُ كِتَابٍ: People of the Book, a recognized scriptural community in this context
key_terms.دِيَةِ ٱلْيَهُودِ وَ ٱلنَّصَارَى: the established blood money of Jews and Christians used here as the legal measure
key_terms.دِيَتَهُمْ: their blood money or legal compensation for killing
key_terms.ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ: Bahrayn, the place to which Khālid ibn al-Walīd was sent
key_terms.ٱلْمَجُوسِ: the Magians, discussed here regarding legal status and compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money of the Magians, and are they considered People of the Book in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the diyyah of the Magians is the same as that of the Jews and Christians. It also explicitly describes them as Ahl al-Kitab in this legal context, establishing a ruling relevant to compensation for unlawful killing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5250 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Samaah ibn Mihran who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent Khalid ibn Al-Walid to Bahrain, where he was involved in shedding the blood of some Jews, Christians, and Magians.

Khalid wrote to the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family), saying:
"I have shed the blood of some Jews and Christians, and I paid their blood money (diyyah) as eight hundred (dirhams) each. I also shed the blood of some Magians, but you did not give me any prior instruction regarding them."
The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) wrote back to him: "Their blood money is the same as that of the Jews and Christians," and he added, "They are People of the Book."
